notes.title: Seamless Discord and Wolfram Integration, UI + Speed Improvements and Podcasts!
notes.content:
Our team has made a long overdue update to the game in celebration of our non-profit's latest release, Trade Bots!

Along with several bug fixes, performance improvements and upgrades to modern frameworks, we've added several new features, all in widescreen mode. (by default, the game opens in a vertical window, but you can full screen the game by hitting the expand button on all three platforms). 


 Wolfram links no longer open externally, instead they open directly within the calculator viewport and can be controlled within the game. 
 Discord has been integrated natively (using the above method). We had honestly not been that familiar or comfortable with discord, but have come to find it's a wonderful way to engage directly with the community. We're closely monitoring the server and hope it continues to thrive. 
 Embeds of some of our favorite podcasts are now integrated directly into the game for you to listen to while playing or making your own levels. 
 The UI in wide mode has changed to include six buttons instead of four.
 New keybindings to make the game even more friendly on desktop.


Thank you so much for playing and for your continued support of educational gaming. Please consider trying the free demo of our latest game, Trade Bots and reading about its development here.

notes.title: New Game Mode and UI Improvements!
notes.content:
Hi Everyone,

This is Chris, the lead developer. I'm so pleased to announce that after a considerable hiatus, we were able to find the time and resources to integrate a few features we've been wanting to add for a long time.  One of the biggest points of feedback we received was the somewhat tedious menu system - we made an artistic decision to try and go for an analog / diegetic feel with the menus, and that became frustrating for players, particularly with the DLC content. The first thing we did was create a simple action sheet that can be accessed by holding down "levels" or by hitting "help" and pressing the "7" key, which now has a hamburger icon on it. 

This menu will provide access to an ordered list of all the DLC levels for easy navigation, as well as.... a new game mode just in time for the school year!

I had always wanted to develop an engine that could procedurally generate levels for the game, but wasn't sure how to approach it. Eventually, I got frustrated and just started tinkering, After a lot of trial and error, this new build represents the first pass at that engine. It doesn't support the OEIS function, and much work needs to be done to improve my approach, but it seemed to give me a good challenge when I was play testing it.

As far as adding more levels to the main game (beyond the DLC) the reality is that very few players, extremely few in fact, are ever able to finish the main campaign - so we thought taking the approach of building an engine that can adapt to a difficulty the player is comfortable with and dynamically create new levels would be a better long term goal. 

I'd like to stress that this new play mode was done in a kind of wonky way,  I'm almost a bit embarrassed to share the code (which I will update soon) because it does some sloppy things and gets semi-mixed results, so I welcome any ideas on how to better generate levels. I'll go into detail on how it works in a later post that I'll make sure to share here. 

Also, out of an abundance of caution, I've created a new public branch called "previous" where the previous build can be accessed just in case there are some bugs. We obviously play tested a fair amount, but you never know! 

Last, I'd like to say I love this game, and have loved my time working on it. I am so thankful to the rich community of players who have engaged with the project and supported us. Your involvement and feedback has been invaluable and is always deeply appreciated. Please feel free to reach out to our non-profit any time (info@cinqmarsmedia.org) or on twitter at @cinqmarsmedia. We always love to hear from you, even if you're just saying "hi"!

My Deepest Thanks,
          - Chris

notes.title: PAX, MoMath and new free DLC!
notes.content:
Hi Everyone!

Thrilled to share with you all that the  Devil's Calculator was a selected as one of the PAX 10 indie games of this year. If you're going to be in Seattle Friday August 30th through Monday September 2nd, please stop to say hi! 

Additionally, we were recently featured at the Museum of Mathematics in New York City where I gave an in-depth presentation on the game for their MOVES conference. Highlights of the talk and new level tutorials can be seen here

We also have a brand new free DLC level (one of my personal favorites) from the great Alex Bellos, bestselling author, numberphile regular and guardian puzzle contributor. 

The latest update features several bug fixes including improved font smoothing and faster performance. Thanks for all your support of this project and educational gaming in general! You guys are the best!

- Chris

notes.title: Version 4.0 Live, More Free DLC and New Features
notes.content:
Hi Everyone! 

Excited to share our newest update with the community:


 New DLC by Tony Padilla and other mathematicians
 Deeper integration with Wolfram Alpha including custom hints, notebooks and scatterplots
 Wolfram MathWorld resources for all puzzles
 Interactive Tutorial added for first level
 Improved BigInt performance across the game
 Bug Fixes including issues with data persistence for DLC and community levels
 Wolfram Cloud API integration for advanced functionality


Our volunteers have been hard at work and trying to roll out an update every month or so with bug fixes, new features, and great new levels by your favorite mathematicians! Follow @devliscalc for updates and thank you, from the bottom of our hearts, for your support and engagement with the project!

notes.title: Major Update: Version 3.0 with Free DLC
notes.content:
Hi Everyone! 

So thrilled and grateful for the positive feedback we've been getting on the game - we never expected it would gain such a following. We've been working around the clock to add tons of new features asked for by the community and lots of stability improvements, all outlined below! 


 Free DLC section added with levels by famous mathematicians like James Tanton and James Grime! 
 Tons of changes under the hood for vastly improved performance and responsiveness, - bottom to top refactoring plus lots and lots of bug fixes
 Ability to create and play community levels without beating the game.
 Community level system completely overhauled, now runs on Math.js:: this means levels can be far more sophisticated (i.e. complex numbers) with less programming and more intuitive syntax. Also far more stable and safer. 
 Ability to copy formula history to the clipboard (by popular demand ːsteamhappyː)
 More seamless Wolfram alpha integration
 More intuitive menu design
 Lots of other subtle improvements and optimizations. 
 Better help resources, including a new User Guide


I still feel such a moron about the two hour downtime on launch day ːsteamfacepalmː (since isolated so it can never happen again). Really excited to share this new version with all of you and I appreciate your support and interest more than you realize.

Please contact me with any issues or questions at info@cinqmarsmedia.com
